prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: fine-line architectural illustration for the Chinese heritage collection 访古. Image 1 is the STYLE MASTER, the Vairocana Buddha contour drawing. Match its delicate organic fine black contours, spare confident lines and large white areas; do not draw Buddha. Image 2 is SUBJECT GEOMETRY ONLY: the actual Yuan offering pavilion (献殿) of Jiutian Shengmu Temple in Donghe village, Pingshun, Shanxi, seen from its LONG SIDE. Preserve the visible FIVE side bays between SIX chamfered stone columns, fully open colonnade, large single hipped roof with very short central ridge and small finial, broad deep projecting eave and roof-end ornaments, bracket sets below eave, low stone platform and some simply outlined ancient stone steles between columns. This is the long side elevation, not its three-bay gableward courtyard approach. Keep the specific photographed proportions and ornaments. Correct camera roll and exaggerated low-angle perspective into a calm side elevation, verticals vertical, entire structure complete. Remove adjacent temples, modern metal support post, bins, wiring, barrels, people and sky. Don't add doors or enclose the pavilion. Draw BLACK INK ON PURE WHITE, no color, no gold, all surfaces WHITE. Thin contours and only sparse roof directions, NOT tile/brick grids. No dark openings, hatching, grey shading or dense texture. Keep steles as 5 or 6 very simple blank silhouettes with thin outlines, no inscriptions. Landscape 1536x1024, complete pavilion occupies about 82% width with generous margins, roof tips and platform uncut. No text, watermarks, captions, dimensions, arrows or borders.
